diagnostic_evidence.quote: $Q$ has an orthonormal basis of eigenfunctions $\{f_k\}_{k = 1}^{\infty}$, spanning $\mathcal{L}^2(\mathcal{D})$, with corresponding eigenvalues $\{\lambda_k\}_{k = 1}^{\infty}$
$e_k = f_k$ for all $k$, i.e., $A$ and $Q$ have a joint basis of eigenfunctions.

issues.failure_explanation: Under parts (i) and (ii) alone, $e_k$ need not be a $Q$-eigenfunction, so the variance of $\langle W_Q(t),e_k\rangle$ need not be $t\lambda_k$. Consequently the normalization by $\sqrt{\lambda_k}$ need not produce a standard Wiener process, and the displayed coefficient formula with that factor is unjustified. Positivity of $\lambda_k$ is also needed for the definition.

failure_location.quote: Assume that \Cref{assumption:operator}(i) and \Cref{assumption:operator}(ii) holds and that $\{X(t)\}_t$ satisfies \Cref{eq:stochastic-convolution}. Define $\omega_k(t) := \frac{1}{\sqrt{\lambda_k}} \inprod{W_Q(t)}{e_k}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require the joint-basis condition in \Cref{assumption:operator}(iii) and positive eigenvalues in the lemma, or reformulate the coordinate noises using the actual covariance matrix.
issues.overall_effect: The lemma is false at its stated level of generality, although later spectral results assume the full joint-eigenbasis assumption.
issues.title: Coefficient representation uses a joint eigenbasis without assuming one
issues.why_classification: Adding the joint-eigenbasis and positivity hypotheses is a short local repair and matches the assumptions already used in the later main results.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Thus $A$ and $Q$ have eigenvalues $\mu_k = r^{-1}(\kappa^2 + \xi_k)^{\alpha}$ and $\lambda_k = \sigma r^{-\gamma}(\kappa^2 + \xi_k)^{-\beta}$ and $\{\mu_k\}_{k = 1}^\infty$ and $\{\lambda_k\}_{k = 1}^{\infty}$ satisfy the bounds $r^{-1} C_\Delta k^{\frac{2 \alpha}{d}}\leq \mu_k$ and $\lambda_k \leq \sigma r^{-\gamma} C_\Delta k^{- \frac{2 \beta}{d}}$.

issues.failure_explanation: Raising the Weyl bound to powers gives $\mu_k\ge r^{-1}C_\Delta^{\alpha}k^{2\alpha/d}$ and $\lambda_k\le \sigma r^{-\gamma}C_\Delta^{-\beta}k^{-2\beta/d}$, not the constants used in the proof. Hence the explicit constant in the corollary does not follow and is generally false, although the exponent in $M$ remains correct.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Recompute $C_1$, $C_2$, and the resulting corollary constant using $C_\Delta^{\alpha}$ and $C_\Delta^{-\beta}$.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised explicit spectral-error constant for the principal elliptic example is unreliable; the convergence rate is unaffected.
issues.title: Laplacian specialization uses incorrect eigenvalue constants
issues.why_classification: This is a local constant recalculation that preserves the hypotheses, convergence rate, and method.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof replaces $\Pi_m g-\Pi_m f_t$ by $\Pi_m(g-f_t)$, which requires additivity and homogeneity. Neither linearity nor an equivalent approximation-stability property is assumed. Reproduction and the displayed norm bound alone allow nonlinear maps that send every nonpolynomial $g+\alpha f_t$ to zero while fixing polynomials; such a map satisfies the stated conditions but its error does not converge.

failure_location.quote: Assume that $\Pi_m$ is such that $\Pi_m g = g$ for all $g \in \mathcal{P}_m(\mathcal{I})$ and that $\Pi_m$ satisfies $\norm{\Pi_m h}_{\mathcal{L}^2([0,t))} \leq C_\Pi \norm{h}_{\mathcal{L}^2([0,t))}$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add linearity of $\Pi_m$ or directly assume the needed quasi-optimality estimate. The concrete projection and point-evaluation maps are linear, so their intended applications remain available.
issues.overall_effect: The general temporal and full-discretization theorems are false for the class of maps they state, and the corollaries cannot follow from the theorem as written.
issues.title: Temporal theorem silently assumes linearity of the approximation map
issues.why_classification: A standard local hypothesis repairs the inference and preserves the concrete schemes, rates, and advertised applications.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof estimates the square root of the mean-square error. Squaring gives factors $\lambda_k$ and, in the improved estimate, $\mu_k^{-2/q}$, not $\sqrt{\lambda_k}$ and $\mu_k^{-1/q}$. At the critical value, the factor $1+\sqrt{\log(th^{-1})}$ must also be squared to obtain the proved mean-square bound. Thus the statements do not match the argument.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Square the root-error estimates consistently, replacing the modal and logarithmic factors throughout the theorem and corollaries; then reconcile all subsequent prose with those corrected bounds.
issues.overall_effect: The modal dependence on $\lambda_k$ and $\mu_k$, and the critical logarithmic factor, are misstated in the temporal theorem and its two direct corollaries. The powers of $h$ away from the logarithmic factor remain unchanged.
issues.title: Mean-square bounds were not squared after estimating the root error
issues.why_classification: The repair is local but materially changes the parameter dependence and critical logarithmic guarantee, so it does not preserve every stated bound even though the principal algebraic time rates survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Thus, if $\theta \in [0,1]$ and $\gamma \leq 1$, or if $\theta \in [0,1)$, we have that

issues.failure_explanation: The comparison used for $(*)$ is multiplied by $2\alpha g_\ell$, whose sign is unrestricted, so the inequality reverses when $\alpha g_\ell<0$. More generally, separate coefficient comparisons do not establish domination between the two quadratic forms because cancellation in $g_\ell+\alpha f_{t_n}$ must be controlled. The final endpoint condition also does not match the lemma's stated condition for $\theta=1$ and $\gamma>1$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Supply a uniform positive-definite quadratic-form or finite-dimensional norm-equivalence argument that handles cancellation and separately treats the last interval and endpoint case.
issues.overall_effect: Uniform $L^2$ stability of the point-sampling operator on the required affine space is not proved, so the convergence guarantee for the left-point method lacks its necessary stability input.
issues.title: Boundedness proof compares signed cross terms as if they were positive
issues.why_classification: A contained but nontrivial stability argument is required; the displayed inequalities cannot be repaired merely by changing a sign.

issues.failure_explanation: A bounded inverse means $\sup_k\mu_k^{-1}<\infty$, not $\sum_k\mu_k^{-1}<\infty$; the displayed finite partial sum is finite for every $M$ regardless. Boundedness of $Q$ only bounds the $\lambda_k$ and therefore does not imply convergence of $\sum_k\mu_k^{-1}\lambda_k$. The needed property is a trace/summability condition such as $A^{-1}Q$ being trace class.

failure_location.quote: In most practical applications $A$ will have bounded inverse, i.e., $\sum_{k = 1}^M \mu_k^{-1} < \infty$, so that in the extreme case of $\gamma > m + \frac{3}{2} + \frac{1}{2}$ we have convergence of $\sum_{k = 1}^M \mu_k^{-1} \lambda_k$ assuming only that $Q$ is bounded.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace bounded invertibility by the explicit summability condition $\sum_k\mu_k^{-1}\lambda_k<\infty$, or by sufficient trace-class assumptions such as summability of $A^{-1}$ together with bounded $Q$.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed uniform-in-$M$ temporal constant for bounded $Q$ is unsupported in the advertised regime.
issues.title: Bounded inverse is confused with summability of inverse eigenvalues
issues.why_classification: The repair requires a materially stronger operator hypothesis and excludes part of the claimed bounded-$Q$ regime, though the formal theorem under explicit summability remains comparable.

issues.failure_explanation: The preceding construction allows nonuniform intervals. The integrals are independent, but the variance on interval $\ell$ is $(1-e^{-2\mu_k h_\ell})/(2\mu_k)$, so they are identically distributed only when all $h_\ell$ are equal.

failure_location.quote: The integrals \linebreak $\{\int_{t_{\ell - 1}}^{t_\ell} \e^{-\mu_k (t_\ell - s)} \, \text{d} \omega_k(s)\}_{\ell = 1}^N$ are then i.i.d. Gaussian variables, with mean $0$ and variance $\int_0^h \e^{-2\mu_k u} \text{d} u = \frac{1}{2 \mu_k} (1 - \e^{-2 \mu_k h})$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either impose a uniform mesh at this point or replace “i.i.d.” by independent Gaussian variables with interval-dependent variances.
issues.overall_effect: The simulation description gives the wrong distributional contract for general meshes, although independent Gaussian sampling remains straightforward.
issues.title: Noise integrals are not identically distributed on a nonuniform mesh
issues.why_classification: This is a short local correction that leaves the algorithm and convergence guarantees intact.
